newsitem.title: UK: Guatemala to hold roadshow for first Eurobond. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Guatemala to hold roadshow for first Eurobond. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]

text.p: Guatemala will begin a series of investor presentations next week before launching its first Eurobond, bankers (corrects the attribution from lead manager BankBoston) said on Thursday.
A syndicate official said the presentations would be held between July 17 and 25 in Europe and the United States, with the bond due to be launched in late July.

As announced by the central bank of Guatemala in April, the bond is expected to be for around $150 million. The syndicate official said it would have a maturity of up to 10 years (corrects from seven to 10-year maturity).
Moody's Investors Service on Tuesday assigned a foreign currency country ceiling of Ba2 for ratings on long-term foreign currency bonds and notes of issuers domiciled in Guatemala.
Moody's said that the ratings reflected Guatemala's improved macroeconomic outlook and its low external debt levels, as well as positive effects from completion of the peace agreements.
